newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Cleaners not protected by EU law, court says.
newsitem.headline: Cleaners not protected by EU law, court says.

text.p: Cleaning ladies are not guaranteed a job with a new services company if their employer loses a cleaning contract, the European Court of Justice said on Thursday.
The court refused to extend the protection granted by EU law to workers whose companies merge or are bought by another, to people who work for contract cleaning companies.
"The mere loss of a service contract to a competitor cannot indicate the existence of a business transfer," the court said.

Ayse Suezen, who worked for a German cleaning company, had argued that when the company lost its contract to clean a high school in Germany, the workers who had cleaned the school should have been taken on by the new cleaning service.

There have been a number of court cases about just what is covered by the EU law and the European Commission has drafted amendments in an effort to clarify it. They will be discussed by EU social affairs ministers in April.

The court said that for the law to apply, there must be a substantial transfer of assets and employees, and this is not the case where a services contract expires and is renegotiated with another business.

"A simple transfer of a contract will not be enough to make the directive applicable," Karen Banks, a Commission legal expert said. "The directive was to protect transfers of business, but not to protect an activity or contract transfer."
With the loss of a service contract, the service provider did not cease to exist, the court said and a part of its business could not automatically be considered to have been transferred.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: German)
"Safeguarding of employees' rights in the event of transfers of undertakings"
Reference by the Arbeitsgericht, Bonn, for a preliminary ruling between
Zehnacker Gebaudereinigung GmbH Kraqnkenhausservie, Lefarth GmbH, party joined

on the interpretation of Council directive 77/187/EEC of 14 February 1977 on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the safeguarding of employees' rights in the event of transfers of undertakings, businesses or parts of businesses (OJ 1977 L 61, p. 26)

Article 1(1) of Council directive 77/187/EEC of 14 February 1977 on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the safeguarding of employees' rights in the event of transfers of undertakings, businesses or parts of businesses is to be interpreted as meaning that the directive does not apply to a situation in which a person who had entrusted the cleaning of his premises to a first undertaking terminates his contract with the latter and, for the performance of similar work, enters into a new contract with a second undertaking, if there is no concomitant transfer from one undertaking to the other of significant tangible or intangible assets or taking over by the new employer of a major part of the workforce, in terms of their numbers and skills, assigned by his predecessor ot the performance of the contract.
